newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch see EU Mideast role supplementary to US.
newsitem.headline: Dutch see EU Mideast role supplementary to US.

text.p: The European Union wants to share in Middle East peace diplomacy but sees its role as supplementary to that of the United states, Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok said on Thursday.

"The European Union chooses a balanced approach. We want to play a role in the talks in addition to the Americans, not instead of the Americans," Kok told a joint news conference with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
"Taking into account the leading role of the Americans -- but supplementary to the leading role of the Americans -- the Europeans play a role."

Netanyahu was in the Netherlands for political and economic talks with the Dutch, who now hold the revolving EU presidency, although discussions were dominated by the current flare up of Israeli-Palestinian violence.
"The main point on the agenda was the frank and open talks we had about the present situation in the Middle East peace process and the lack of progress," Kok said.
Israel has said European moves at the United Nations to censure its decision to build a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem harmed EU efforts to mediate between it and the Palestinians.
Protesting Palestinians have clashed with Israeli security forces since work started on the settlement on March 18 and Israeli settlers and troops killed three Palestinians in Hebron on Tuesday.
Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo will visit Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Friday as part of the EU's contribution to finding solutions to the problems in the Middle East, Kok said.

"It is our view that of course we should be in close contact with the prime minister and government of Israel at the same time as the Palestinians in order to explore... possibilities for lasting peace," Kok said.
Standing at his side, Netanyahu said the two had discussed the contribution of Europe to the peace process.
"Prime minister Kok has spoken about the fact that Europe works closely with the United States, works closely with us and with the Palestinians," he said.
"I believe with goodwill all these efforts will point in the one single direction we all aspire to, which is the cessation of violence and the resumption of the path to peace."
Netanyahu reiterated Israel's commitment to building housing in East Jerusalem, saying it would benefit both Jews and Palestinians.
"We certainly believe it is our right and responsibility to build housing units for all of Jerusalem's residents, for Arabs and for Jews alike," he said.
Netanyahu was due to address Dutch business leaders in the Hague and meet Dutch Queen Beatrix later on Thursday before going on to Rome on Friday.
